name: First 5K / 10K
summary: Build up to a 5K or 10K with a week-by-week walk-run or run plan, rest days and an easy race week.

onboarding.prompt: Got a race on the calendar?
options: Yes, I have a race date
No race yet, just the distance
onboarding.reaction: Either way works. A date just gives the plan a finish line.

onboarding.prompt: When is the race (or the day you want to run it)?
onboarding.reaction: Marked. We'll count back from there.
Nice. We'll size the weeks to match.

onboarding.prompt: How many times a week do you run or walk-run now?
onboarding.reaction: Zero is a perfectly good starting line.

onboarding.prompt: Longest run or walk in the last month, in minutes?
onboarding.reaction: Good to know. Week one starts a notch below that.

onboarding.prompt: Tap the days and times you're free to run.
onboarding.reaction: Locked in. Runs land there, with rest days in between.

phases.name: Easy start
benchmarks: Three sessions a week for three weeks
actions: Walk-run intervals sized from your longest recent run

phases.name: Build
benchmarks: Run or walk-run 20 to 30 minutes without stopping
Longest run grows by no more than about 10% a week
actions: Three runs a week: easy, steady, longer

phases.name: Race ready
benchmarks: One longer run near race distance
actions: Race day or personal time trial

plan_blueprint.calendar: Three runs a week on the chosen slots, rest days left open, a longer run on the weekend slot, and a lighter race week ending in race day. 5K plans run about 8 weeks; 10K plans about 12.

approach_variants.habit: Runs attached to an existing routine (after school drop-off, before dinner); streak of weeks with three runs.
approach_variants.willpower: Weekly countdown to race day and a stretch target for the longest run, still inside safe weekly increases.
approach_variants.time: Every run is a fixed calendar block with warm-up and cool-down time built in; Sunday time review.
approach_variants.reward: Owner-picked rewards at week 4, week 8 and race day (new socks, a race photo print).
approach_variants.resource: Week one covers shoes, a safe route, a running app or watch if wanted, and a buddy or group.

guardrails: Talk to your doctor before starting. GoalKin offers education, not medical advice.
Stop and rest if you feel pain, dizziness or chest discomfort, and get checked before running again.
Every plan item can be edited, moved or removed, and you can add your own steps.
Product, app or recipe ideas are labeled as suggestions; any affiliate link is disclosed.
restart_rules: One missed run is skipped, not doubled up. Missing a full week repeats the last completed week. Missing two or more weeks offers a re-plan that steps back one phase and moves the race-day target if needed.
